questions.q: How many consistency levels does Cosmos DB offer, and what do they represent?
options: Five levels, forming a real spectrum between strict correctness (Strong) and low latency/high availability (Eventual)
Two levels: consistent and inconsistent
Three levels, identical to SQL Server's transaction isolation levels
One fixed level that cannot be changed
questions.explain: Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session, Consistent Prefix, and Eventual form a genuine spectrum, not an arbitrary list.

options: Every read returns the most recent committed write, at the cost of the highest latency and availability impact
Reads may return data from up to 24 hours ago
Writes are guaranteed to fail if any region is unreachable
It guarantees the fastest possible read latency
questions.explain: Strong is the strictest guarantee — always the latest committed write — which is exactly why it costs the most in latency and availability.

questions.q: What does Session consistency guarantee, and why is it the default?
options: Read-your-writes and monotonic reads within a client session, matching how most applications actually behave, at low latency
That every client in every region sees identical data at every instant
That writes are never lost, but reads can return data from any point in history
It guarantees strict ordering across all clients globally
questions.explain: Session guarantees a client always sees its own writes and never sees data move backward — the practical sweet spot for most real applications.

questions.q: What does Consistent Prefix guarantee that Eventual consistency does not?
options: That reads never see writes out of order, even though they may lag behind the most recent write
That reads are always fully up to date
That writes across regions are merged instantly
That every read is billed at zero RU cost
questions.explain: Consistent Prefix preserves write order (no gaps or reordering) but doesn't guarantee freshness, unlike Eventual which guarantees neither.

questions.q: Can an individual request override the account's default consistency level, and if so, how?
options: Yes — a request can ask for a weaker consistency level than the account default, but never a stronger one
No, the consistency level can never be changed per request
Yes, a request can always ask for a stronger level than the account default
Only the Eventual level can ever be requested, regardless of the account default
questions.explain: The account sets the default, but individual requests may relax it to something weaker when appropriate for that specific call.
